name: Question 12
problem:
Consider a function $b(t)$ such that its Laplace transform is $L{b(t)}=B(s)$ for $s>{s}_{0}.$ Suppose we wish to find $L{{e}^{t}b(t)}.$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below.By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write 

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{t}b(t)} & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-1}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-2}}\,b(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={{field-3}}\,\text{for}\,{{field-4}}.\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
Starting from the definition of the Laplace transform, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{t}b(t)} & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\cdot {e}^{t}\,b(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-(s-1)t}\,b(t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $B(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-st}\,b(t)\,\text{d}t,$ where $s>{s}_{0}.$ Therefore, 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-(s-1)t}\,b(t)\,\text{d}t=B(s-1),
$$

where 

$$
s-1>{s}_{0}\,⇒\,s>{s}_{0}+1.
$$

Question 12
?
Consider a function b(t) such that its Laplace transform is L{b(t)}=B(s) for s>s0. Suppose we wish to find L{etb(t)}. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write

 
e−st⋅etb(t)
est⋅etb(t)
e−st⋅e−tb(t)
est⋅e−tb(t)
 
e(s+1)t
e−(s+1)t
e(s−1)t
e−(s−1)t
 
B(s−1)
B(s)
B(s+1)
 
s>s0−1
s>s0+1
s>s0
L{etb(t)}=∫0∞{(e−st⋅etb(t))(S0)}dt=∫0∞{(e(s+1)t)(S1)}b(t)dt={(B(s−1))(S2)}for{(s>s0−1)(S3)}.

Submit

EXPLANATION

Starting from the definition of the Laplace transform, we have

L{etb(t)}=∫0∞e−st⋅etb(t)dt=∫0∞e−(s−1)tb(t)dt

Now, recall that B(s)=∫0∞e−stb(t)dt, where s>s0. Therefore, ∫0∞e−(s−1)tb(t)dt=B(s−1), where s−1>s0⇒s>s0+1.
